description: Hi everyone! I'm a Chemical Engineer passionate about thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics. Inspired by the Columbia Shuttle disaster, my PHOENIX contribution is to investigate how a small ignition event can trigger fire propagation and explore engineering solutions to contain it before it spreads. I'm excited to use NASA's research and datasets to help develop a practical fire-prevention concept for space environments!
summary:
PHOENIX is an engineering research and decision-support prototype designed to help improve spacecraft safety by organizing NASA research on fire hazards and external vehicle integrity. It brings together two complementary intelligence domains: Internal Fire Intelligence, which examines material-specific fire behavior, ignition, flame propagation, smoke, and suppression; and External Integrity Intelligence, which considers thermal protection, insulation, and potential structural damage.

PHOENIX uses NASA research and experimental evidence to support condition-aware comparisons across materials and operating environments. Rather than applying one generic model, it emphasizes the importance of material properties, geometry, oxygen concentration, airflow, and experimental conditions. The prototype aims to help researchers interpret evidence, identify relevant hazards, and make more informed engineering decisions for future human spaceflight.
details:
How PHOENIX Works

PHOENIX (Proactive Hazard Observation, Isolation and Extinction Network for eXtreme Environments) is an interactive research and engineering decision-support prototype focused on spacecraft fire safety and external vehicle integrity.

The prototype organizes NASA combustion research into a structured environment where users can explore investigations, compare experimental conditions, and examine evidence relevant to spacecraft safety.

Two Complementary Engineering Domains

1. Internal Fire Intelligence

This domain focuses on fire hazards inside crewed spacecraft. It considers ignition conditions, material-specific flame behavior, propagation, smoke generation, detection, suppression, extinction and potential reignition.

2. External Integrity Intelligence

This separate domain explores spacecraft thermal-protection systems, insulation and impact-related damage. It recognizes that external structural and thermal hazards require different evidence and engineering approaches from cabin fire analysis.

Scientific and Engineering Approach

PHOENIX emphasizes material-specific and condition-aware interpretation. Relevant experimental factors include material composition, geometry, thickness, oxygen concentration and partial pressure, total pressure, airflow, ventilation configuration and ignition conditions.

The research framework references NASA investigations including BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I, SAME-R, SPICE, ACME and FLEX. It is designed to help users preserve experimental context rather than apply one generic model to different materials or combustion environments.

Prototype Features

The current interactive prototype includes:

  • A NASA research catalogue with links to relevant investigations.
  • An internal fire evidence interface.
  • A BASS-II PMMA experimental comparison example with a metadata compatibility check.
  • An external integrity research interface.
  • A materials dashboard.
  • A curated scientific interpreter and guided research prompts.
  • An interactive research dashboard with transparent, rule-based relevance ranking.

The dashboard's scores represent topic relevance only. They are not fire-risk, flammability, experimental-quality or mission-safety predictions.

Tools and Development

The project is presented as a web-based interactive prototype, maintained in a public GitHub repository and deployed through GitHub Pages. NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository is its primary scientific research reference.

Innovation and Intended Impact

PHOENIX brings multiple NASA research investigations into one mission-oriented engineering environment. Its central innovation is the emphasis on traceable evidence, experimental metadata compatibility and material-specific reasoning.

The long-term vision is to develop a research assistant that can help engineers discover, compare and interpret scientific evidence more efficiently. Automated NASA PSI ingestion and a connected generative-AI scientific interpreter are future development goals, not operational features of the current prototype.

PHOENIX is an early-stage research and engineering prototype. It is not a certified spacecraft fire-safety system, and mission-critical decisions require validated models and qualified human engineering review.
